# NOTES ON THE TEXT (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 (main book): "Dick Merriwell's Heroic Players; or, How the Yale Nine Won the Championship" by Burt L. Standish (Street & Smith, copyright 1912; Merriwell Series; publisher's blurb pages precede it)

### Front matter (ads, not story)
- Merriwell series ad: "101–208" titles listed; forthcoming 209–221 (Jan–June 1929), incl. 211 "Dick Merriwell's Heroic Players" (Feb 1929), 212 "Dick Merriwell at the Olympics" (next title, per end note).
- Alger Series list (1–36), Nick Carter New Magnet Library list (901–1264), Tales of the Rolling Plains/Great Western Library (Diamond Dick, Buffalo Bill; 1–65), Round the World Library (Jack Harkaway, 1–117). Not part of Heroic Players story.

### Characters (Heroic Players)
- **Dick Merriwell**: Yale universal coach, former captain; respected; "inside baseball" lessons; boxer; lumber interests in Maine with Chester Arlington (engineer, Valdivia; sister June).
- **Jim Phillips**: Yale sophomore pitcher (later junior, elected baseball captain at end); "best college pitcher"; curves, control, cross-fire ball; plays left-arm drop at end of Harvard game; kidnapped in Boston cab; escapes by aviation (biplane from Squantum); locked in freight car (rescued via Foote's ventriloquism trap); sinks *Marina* by punching hole; cleared of bank robbery charge.
- **Bill Brady**: sophomore catcher, big, "Bill"; slugger; afraid of high ball (fixed by Jim); son of wealthy man (father buys Elm National control; telegram gives authority).
- **Harry Maxwell**: former roommate of Jim; outfielder.
- **Sam Taylor**: senior catcher, former football tackle; formerly enemy of Jim; falsely accused of cribbing.
- **Bob Gray**: senior pitcher, Taylor's roommate; falsely accused of blank history exam paper; strikes out three Harvard batters in commencement game.
- **Tom Sherman**: senior captain of baseball team, first baseman; sails to Europe later.
- **Steve Carter**: third baseman; once plotted against Jim; reformed; nominates Jim as captain.
- **Jack Tempest**: Virginian sprinter; Jim's friend; overheard Parker's insults.
- **Woeful Watson**: sophomore class pessimist; "first catch your rabbit"; rows Jim; locked-freight-car companion.
- **Jackson**: second baseman; junior; football quarterback; later football captain.
- **Hasbrook**: New Haven Country Club captain; old Yale man.
- **Winston**: substitute pitcher; pitches Commencement Day game.
- **Caxton** (center fielder), **Horton** (shortstop), **Brayson**, **Tuthill**, **Green** (country club).
- **Gurney**: sophomore bettor. **Carpenter**: bespectacled grind, glasses; plotter; confesses. **Shesgren**: small sophomore, glasses, blue eyes, thin voice; go-between with Chetwind; tied up by Parker; turns on plot.
- **Wesley Parker**: junior, big guard, football candidate; drinker; villain; plotter; ends in confession, withdraws from captaincy; suspected in kidnapping (Foote); later "seen what it meant to be a Yale man."
- **Paul Foote**: undersized junior, cigarette smoker; father rowed crew 25 years ago; villain; plotter (blank exam paper frame, freight car trap, gambling debts); caught by finger prints on bread; confesses.
- **Danby**: former football captain who left college.
- **Chetwind**: New Haven real-estate broker, country club member; sent $100 via registered letter (two $50 bills); later confirms Shesgren was go-between; described Parker.
- **Bowen**: Harvard senior captain, catcher; Andover friend of Brady; files protest; withdraws it.
- **Briggs**: Harvard pitcher ("control"); pitches Amherst shutout.
- **Wooley**: Harvard ace (last year).
- **Hobson**: famous former Harvard pitcher; pitched Boston Athletic Association team.
- **Reid**: Harvard shortstop/batter; hits game-tying/near-winning drive in final game; struck out in later game.
- **Farquar**, **Renshaw**, **Hazlitt**, **Morgan**: Harvard players.
- **Neilson**: Harvard crew coach; honest; "John Harvard" launch. **Thompson**: young Harvard coach.
- **Benton** and **Hargreaves**: Yale graduate assistant crew coaches.
- **Murchison**: crew captain/stroke; **Flagg**: number seven; **Rogers**: coxswain; **Harper**: bow.
- **Canfield**: professor, history exam; "Professor Canfield."
- **Dean** (unnamed); **Gordon**: instructor who received Foote's tip.
- **Sam** (old rubber, "Marse Dick").
- **Detective Jones**: New Haven police; fingerprint evidence.
- **Joseph Bromlow**: president of Elm National Bank; **Hastings**: cashier. **Riggs**: paying teller, stole $1000, later confesses; suspended sentence.
- **Marsten** ("Johnny", "Bunny"): gambler, gambling house in New Haven; keeps stolen goods; later closed.
- **Harding** (Bill Harding): gambler, New York political pull; old enemy of Dick; father New Haven boss, dying in asylum; falsely framed/blamed; jumped by Jim in New London.
- **Barrows** (Pete): professional gambler, villain; plan to rig boat race; sentenced to 5 years.
- **Svenson**: captain of schooner *Marina* (Gloucester, Mass.), drinker, Norse; loses boat.
- **Dennison**: weak investor; **Barnes**: Harding's agent; **Bascom**: electrician/ex-wireless operator; slingshot; bank heist.
- **Phelps**: financier, Maine lumber opponent; pays Barrows $5000 to ruin Dick.
- **Sam Taylor's girl letters**; **Captain Svenson**.
- **Foote's father**: threatens to cut him off.
- **Alexander/"Bert"** none.

### Plot events (in order)
1. Ch I: Bill and Jim practice high-ball hitting vs Harvard pitcher Briggs (Bowen catching, Harvard captain). Dick Merriwell praises them.
2. Ch II: Gurney bets; Watson pessimism; Carpenter (grind) and Shesgren resent Jim; Parker (junior, football) overhears; proposes plot; Tempest insults-exchange.
3. Ch III: Hasbrook (country club) asks Jim to pitch vs Boston Athletic Association (Hobson). Dick consents on conditions. Parker, drinking, with Carpenter and Shesgren at club porch; sends them to Jim; hands letter to stranger.
4. Ch IV: Brady, Jim discuss Carpenter visit; Jim finds one registered letter (second vanished). Game at club: Jim and Hobson pitch; Yale wins (Hasbrook winning run, Boston dropped ball).
5. Ch V: Dick explains Boston infield shift (Jimmy Collins trick). Dick at football election (Parker vs Jackson vs Jones); Sherman & Taylor get it postponed for Danby. Bowen files protest: Phillips professional; Chetwind receipt, $100.
6. Ch VI: Chetwind refuses to name agent; Jim denies; missing second registered letter; receipt signed by Jim.
7. Ch VII: Parker announces charge publicly; Carter reveals; Dick believes conspiracy.
8. Ch VIII: Parker tells Carpenter/Shesgren; ties Shesgren, takes money, marks bills; plants letter.
9. Ch IX: Jim/Brady find letter with no money (note paper) in room; post-office inspector; Chetwind names Shesgren; Shesgren description.
10. Ch X: Shesgren confesses; Dick confronts Parker; knife nick proof; Parker confesses and withdraws; Carpenter confesses; Jim forgives.
11. Ch XI: Boston trip; Jim kidnapped in taxicab (Brady goes into drugstore); taken to seashore.
12. Ch XII: Jim escapes via biplane from Squantum, lands at Harvard field; Yale wins first game 1–0 (Carter steals, Brady fly; wild pitch play with cap; Farquar tagged out).
13. Ch XIII: Parker withdraws; Foote and Parker plot; Gray/Taylor cribbing plot.
14. Ch XIV: Dick confronts Parker; Parker's false apology; steals blue confession sheet (Tempest sees, Marching through Georgia).
15. Ch XV: Foote switches confession; Parker tears it up.
16. Ch XVI: Dick finds crib notes (Sam Taylor's name; Gray's name); Taylor denies.
17. Ch XVII: Dean; Foote tipped Gordon; Foote's secret entry into Dwight Hall.
18. Ch XVIII: Commencement Day (June); Gray forbidden to pitch (blank exam); Winston pitches; Harvard wins 3–? ; Gray appears in ninth; series tied.
19. Ch XIX: Dick proves via finger prints (police, Gray's prints differ); Foote's leaves hidden in catalogue.
20. Ch XX: Parker and Foote; leaves missing; Foote plans to remove Jim.
21. Ch XXI: Jim locked in freight car at New Haven freight yard (Foote's ventriloquism cry).
22. Ch XXII: Parker found; Foote caught by bread-print fingerprints; car number 34576 Big Four; Jim found at Kingston NY; Turkish bath.
23. Ch XXIII: Final Yale-Harvard game at Polo Grounds; Yale wins 3–2; Jim triple play with left hand; Jim elected captain.
24. Ch XXIV–XXV: Crew trouble; freshmen beat varsity; plot with Svenson/Barrows on *Marina*; odds.
25. Ch XXVI–XXVIII: Crew trials; Harvard also slow; Dick's watch from Thompson; investigation; Harding on Marina.
26. Ch XXIX: Jim jumps Harding; Brady arrives; Harding leaves New London.
27. Ch XXX: Jim overhears wireless (Ma, Ma, Ma); caught; held on Marina.
28. Ch XXXI: Jim finds magnet coil; model shell with iron groove.
29. Ch XXXII: Jim scuttles Marina with mallet; escapes; coil found in both shells; shells replaced.
30. Ch XXXIII–XXXIV: Race; Yale wins four-oar, freshmen, varsity by <2 sec; Barrows's clockwork torpedo stopped by Jim in hydroplane.
31. Ch XXXV: Olympics talk; Boston challenge for rematch; Jim pitch, Brady catcher; Dick captains New Haven team.
32. Ch XXXVI–XL: Foote gambling; Marsten; Barrows recruits Foote; Riggs bank theft; Bascom; combinations; bank night plot.
33. Ch XLI: Jim sees watchman shot; bank rob foiled; Jim slugged; Barrows & Bascom escape; tramp freight train.
34. Ch XLII–XLIV: Jim found in vault; counterfeit $5000 deposited by Dick; Brady telegram; Barrows arrested; Riggs confesses; Barrows 5 years; Foote confesses.
35. Ch XLV: July 4 rematch vs Boston; Briggs; Jim's arm falters; bunt tactics; Jim out on appeal; New Haven wins 8–7; end.

### Key numbers/quotes
- Phillips: "Jim"; Yale vs Harvard series two games; 1st game at Cambridge Yale won 1–0 (per text); Commencement game Harvard won; final game Yale won; Boston rematch 8–7.
- Registered letter: $100 (two $50 bills), Chetwind; Dick's deposit $5000 (fifty $100 bills).
- Boat race: Yale wins by <2 sec; four-oar Yale by <2 sec; freshmen by ten lengths.
- Car number 34,576 (text says "thirty-four thousand five hundred and seventy-six"), Big Four Road.
- Parker's whistled tune: "Marching Through Georgia."
- Hasbrook winning run; Briggs/Bowen; Brady "I'll eat my hat."

## BOOK 2–5 (ads/listings, no story)
- Alger Series, Nick Carter New Magnet Library, Great Western Library (Diamond Dick/Buffalo Bill), Round the World Library (Jack Harkaway). Titles only; no narrative.
